newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols soften as bonds drift back up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols soften as bonds drift back up.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options softened as the underlying market drifted back up in the afternoon after tumbling earlier from overnight highs, traders said.

In addition to the weekend time-decay pressure, bids were dampened by perception that the bond market could be in a more consolidative range-trading for a while after its selloff from early August highs.
But prevailing nervousness, reflected in the market's wild roller-coaster ride in recent sessions, underpinned volatilities on the whole, traders noted.
"I've never seen this market whip around so much," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.

September T-bond futures fell to a low of 112-27/32 in early trade after climbing to a high of 113-27/32 overnight. They subsequently clawed their way back up to settle at 113-20/32, unchanged from Thursday.

The market had shown similar erratic behavior in the previous few days. Hangover from last week's Treasury refunding and caution ahead of next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting were seen to be the main destabilization factor.
Implied volatility for October T-bond futures options stood at around 8.0 percent in late trade, off more than a quarter point on the day. December was little changed at around 8.5 percent.
Implied volatility for September options, which expire next Friday, fluctuated wildly and pricing levels were difficult to assess, particularly when the bond market was moving around, traders said.
For instance, an investment bank was seen buying 3,000 contracts of September 113 puts when futures were about to dip below 113 and implied volatility was pumped up.
"They paid 34 up to 45 (34/64 to 45/64 points in premium), which were the highs," the brokerage trader said. "They paid way too much and the market came right back."

Among other big trades of the day, a German house was seen buying 2,000 contracts of September 115 calls early in the day and a further 2,000 contracts in the afternoon after the bond market began edging back up.
At the shorter end, Eurodollar volatilities were mostly steady. Volatilities for December and March Eurodollar futures options were flat to 0.1 point easier at 8.4 and 10.6 percent respectively.
A brokerage Eurodollar trader said Eurodollar futures appeared to have put in a bottom and there was little fear that the Fed would raise rates next week.
"We're not really seeing people build up positions for FOMC," he said.
December Eurodollar futures ended 4.5 basis points higher at 94.140.
